accessNote.text:
People and access: Users, Roles, Classification

• The three pages share a row of links under the top bar; the sidebar’s Users entry opens the section until the full Administration menu exists.
• Roles: open a role to see its permissions (built-in roles are read-only). New and Edit list every permission in five groups, with the Admin (needs two-step sign-in) and Per unit tags. Remove only works for roles nobody holds.
• Editing a role that people hold says that changes apply to them at once.
• Classification: up and down move a level one place; the arrows point where the row goes (the app’s arrows point the other way today). A new level goes in as the most sensitive, as the API does.
• Refusals show inside the dialog: name taken, still in use, last level, at most 20 levels, changed meanwhile. Every change asks for step-up first.
• API: tenant.settings.manage has no label in the web catalogue yet (shown here as “Manage organisation settings”). Nothing else new.

apiChanges.text:
API changes this design needs

Inbox (GET /api/v1/inbox/tasks)
1. Counts — total open tasks for the My tasks tab, the sidebar Inbox badge and the "x of N selected" footer.
2. Action per task — DECIDE does not say whether the step is Approve or Recommend.
3. Memo type — add the memo type's name to InboxMemo.
4. Sender — who sent the task (previous holder or author).
5. Filters — text (subject or reference), memo type, due (overdue / due soon / none), working with sort and the cursor.

Notifications (GET /api/v1/me/notifications)
6. Filters — unread only, and category (approvals, following, security, administration), working with the cursor.
7. Context — the second line needs a little more in params: the memo subject, a snippet of the note that mentions you, the sign-in place and browser.

Watching (GET /api/v1/inbox/watching)
8. Status — add the memo's status to WatchingItem, so the list can show In review / Approved / Closed without opening each memo.

Any request (all of /api/v1)
9. Session ended — when a session has ended (timed out, signed out elsewhere, or ended from My security), answer 401 with a problem reason that says so, e.g. SESSION_ENDED, so the app shows “You were signed out” instead of “Something went wrong”.

Last seen (memo view, inbox, watching)
10. Last seen — record when a person opens a memo (per person, per memo). The memo view returns lastSeenAt and what changed since: resubmission and its remark, document versions, attachments added, notes added, and the person's own last action (e.g. their return remark).
11. Unread — inbox task and watching items carry unread: true when the memo has news since the person last opened it. Opening the memo clears it.
Next task and the reading pane need nothing new: they follow the inbox order the client already has, fetching the next page by cursor when needed.

Admin pages (/api/v1/admin)
Nothing new. Each area note says what it reads; the overview’s “Waiting for you” reads existing lists, in several calls.

Operator console (/api/v1/platform)
12. Organisations list — hasAdmin on each row (today only the single view has it), and status and hasAdmin filters, for the Administrator column and the All / Active / Suspended / No administrator tabs.
13. Platform audit — the organisation’s name with each entry that concerns one, so the Object column can name it and link to it.

behaviour.text:
Behaviour notes

• Team tab appears only for people who oversee a unit (as today); everyone else sees five tabs.
• Organisation name and logo come from tenant branding; it is a label, not a switcher.
• Under the user's name we show the email: the user record has no job title.
• Row "⋯" menu: Claim, Release, Watch for that one task (existing endpoints).
• Show more loads the next batch by cursor; 50 per batch on desktop, 25 on phones.
• Forms validate in the app (TanStack Form), never with browser HTML validation: noValidate on every form, our own messages under the field, focus to the first error, submit stays enabled.
• New states the app does not handle yet: Page not found (unknown address), No access to this page (a page the person’s roles do not allow; today the API answers 403), Connection lost (offline bar) and Signed out (session ended mid-task). See the Page states row.
• Next task: “Open my next task after this” sits in every decision dialog, on by default and remembered per person. It follows My tasks in its current sort and filters, and skips restricted and blocked tasks. After the last one: “That was your last task: My tasks is clear.” and back to Inbox.
• Opened from My tasks, the memo header shows “1 of 7 in My tasks” with previous and next (J and K).
• Since you last looked: shown on a memo you have opened before when something changed. It starts with what you asked for last time, then resubmission, document versions (with Compare), attachments and new notes. Notes added since your last visit carry a “New” tag on the note sheet.
• Unread: a blue dot and a heavier subject on My tasks and Watching rows; screen readers hear “Unread”. Opening the memo clears it.
• Reading pane: off by default. A “Reading pane” switch in the My tasks toolbar (shown at 1400px and wider) turns it on; the choice is remembered per person. When on, the list and the selected memo sit side by side with the same decision buttons. Links from notifications, search and Home still open the full page; narrower screens and phones always use list → page.

buildNote.text:
Build note

Use shadcn/ui components for everything: Button, Input, InputOTP, Select, Combobox, Tabs, Table, Dialog, Drawer, AlertDialog, DropdownMenu, Popover, Badge, Skeleton, Alert, Sonner, Sidebar. These boards are hand-written HTML only because the canvas cannot run React; do not copy their inline styles. The component for each pattern is listed on the Design rules page, section 1.

memoAdminNote.text:
Memos: Memo types, Numbering, Distribution lists

• The three pages share a row of section links; the sidebar’s Memo types entry opens the section.
• Memo types list: tabs In use / Switched off and a filter by name or code, worked out in the browser (the list is small). Switching off asks first and says memos already written keep the type.
• Editor: one page per type with a version picker. The tweak “state” shows a draft (Save, Submit for review), a version in review (Changes tab first; remark, Send back, Approve and publish) and a published version (read-only, New draft). Only a draft can change; reviewing needs a second administrator, and publishing asks for step-up.
• Form tab: fields in order with move, edit, remove, and the template with its tags; the preview shows the form as the author will see it.
• Numbering tab: number parts, series, restart, count and when the number is given, with a sample of the next numbers.
• Numbering page: series on the left, the chosen counter’s register on the right, with the completeness check and void numbers. “Set a starting number” offers Unit only for series counted per unit, as a unit picker instead of a unit id.
• Distribution lists: members as people or positions; a position reaches whoever holds it when a copy is sent. A name and at least one member are checked separately.
• API: nothing new. The memo type filter and tabs are client-side.

operatorTodo.text:
Operator console: all six pages designed

• A separate app for the people who run the platform. Its top bar stays dark in both themes and says Memo & Meetings · Platform administration, with its two pages (Organisations, Platform audit), the operator and Sign out. Pages are full width, like the admin pages.
• Sign-in and two-step setup use the organisation sign-in frame (the platform pages share its AuthLayout): language and theme at the top, the product inside the card. A new operator arrives through a one-time link from the server: choose a password, then set up two-step sign-in. An expired link says what to do. Operators have no recovery codes, so the code screen says who can reset it.
• Organisations: status tabs (All, Active, Suspended, No administrator) and search, like Users; the registry table; “N shown” and Show more. Operators see registry entries only, never what is inside an organisation.
• New organisation is a page with “What happens” beside the form, and shows the web address as it is typed.
• Suspending asks for the organisation’s address to be typed (new): it locks everyone out at once. Resume asks first. Suspended is a warning (amber), like a locked account.
• Create, Suspend, Resume and Send invitation ask “Confirm it is you” with a code first, as the server requires (the `stepUp` dialog tweak on New organisation and Organisation detail).
• Platform audit has the same filters and columns as the organisation’s Audit (From, To, Action starts with; Time, Who, Action, Object). Organisations in it link to their page.
• API: the Administrator column and the Suspended and No administrator tabs need hasAdmin and a status filter on the list (today hasAdmin is only on the single view); audit entries need the organisation’s name. Everything else exists.

overviewNote.text:
Administration overview and the grouped menu

• The overview is the full Administration menu: all 18 entries of app/navigation.ts in five groups (People and access, Memos, Workflows, Organisation-wide settings, Records), each with one line saying what it is for. People see only the entries their roles allow; the “viewer” tweak shows someone who can only reassign tasks.
• Each section page has a row of links to its siblings, so the sidebar can stay short.
• Proposal for the sidebar’s Administration group: Overview, People and access, Memos, Workflows, Open tasks, Settings, Records, each opening the first page of its section. The boards still show today’s six entries (Overview, Users, Memo types, Workflows, Open tasks, Security).
• “Waiting for you” lists what needs an administrator now: tasks waiting for reassignment, versions to review, failed email, locked accounts. New: it reads existing lists (open tasks, memo types, workflows, mail log, users); no new API, but several calls.

recImportBatchTitle.text: Import batch (metadata, originals, mappings, dry run, import, report)

recordsNote.text:
Records: Audit and Import

• Audit and Import share a row of section links; the sidebar shows them under Overview until the menu changes (see the overview note).
• Audit: the filters of the app (From, To, Action starts with, Object type) above the table; Details opens the before and after of one entry. Export asks first and warns that a filtered export cannot prove nothing is missing.
• Import: batches with their state; one batch is a six-step page (Metadata, Originals, Mappings, Dry run, Import, Report) with done steps ticked. The “run” tweak shows a batch ready to import, importing, stopped, and completed with its reconciliation report.
• Importing asks first and says plainly that imported memos are final and cannot be undone; Abandon and Close need a reason.
• Phones: no folder sending (“Use a computer to send a folder.”); everything else can be followed.
• API: nothing new.

settingsNote.text:
Organisation-wide settings: Security, Email, Branding, Language and terms

• The four pages share a row of section links; the sidebar’s Administration › Security entry opens them.
• Settings pages are forms on the page with a Save bar that stays at the bottom and says when there are unsaved changes. Saving asks for step-up, as the app does. “Someone changed these settings meanwhile” shows in the bar.
• Security: each number shows the range the server allows (for example 5–480); errors sit under the field, including “Lock after more failures than the waiting starts.” A side panel says in plain words what people will notice (new copy).
• Email: the mail server is a summary card with Change (a dialog), Send a test email, and Use the platform’s server (asks first). A failed test shows on the card. The delivery log has All / Failed tabs.
• Branding: logo shown on light and dark, colours with live contrast checks from lib/contrast.ts, and a sign-in preview in both themes.
• Language and terms: default language and time zone; the organisation’s own words per language, with grammatical gender for Arabic and right-to-left fields.
• API: nothing new.

signinTitle.text: Sign in, reset password, two-step setup, invitation

userDetailNote.text:
User detail

• One page for a person: account status and the account actions from the Users list, then positions, roles and clearance (today the app shows only the last three).
• Account actions sit in the header and follow the same rules as the list menu; on phones they are in the ⋯ sheet.
• Clearance opens a dialog with the levels from least to most sensitive, instead of a select on the page.
• Give a role: “Where” is offered only for roles that can be limited to a unit; otherwise it says the role applies to the whole organisation.
• Every change asks for step-up (Confirm it is you) first, as the app does. Refusals (already holds it, last administrator, changed meanwhile) show inside the dialog.
• Needs nothing new from the API: GET /admin/users/{id}, its assignments and access, plus the existing lifecycle endpoints.

wfWorkflowBuilderTitle.text: Workflow builder (diagram, steps, JSON, changes, simulate)

workflowsNote.text:
Workflows: definitions, builder, delegation of authority, queues, substitutions, business calendar

• The five pages share a row of section links; the sidebar’s Workflows entry opens the section. Open tasks keeps its own sidebar entry.
• Builder: the version picker and states work as for memo types (draft, in review, published). Views: Diagram, Steps (the same workflow as a list, for keyboard and screen readers), JSON, and Changes while in review. The side panel shows the selected step, or Simulate. Added, changed, reached and problem steps are marked with a word, never colour alone.
• Check runs the validator and shows the result above the view; Submit is refused with “Fix the problems first.” while there are problems.
• Phones: no diagram (it needs a wider screen); Steps is the default view, and a step opens as a sheet.
• Published version: “Memos on older versions” lists running memos and which can move.
• Delegation of authority: versions, then the selected version’s date and rules (first match applies) with approval groups; “Who approves this?” sits beside it. A rule opens for editing with Change.
• Queues: like distribution lists, with a key that cannot change once made.
• Substitutions: In force / Planned / Ended tabs; Move open tasks and End today. Business calendar: weekly hours, a month view of holidays and special hours, and “When is it due?”.
• API: nothing new. The workflow list tabs and filter are worked out in the browser.

homeDashNote.text:
Home and Dashboard: one job each — implementation

• Home is where everyone starts and acts. The Dashboard is a report for people who oversee a unit. They are not merged: Home loads on every sign-in and must stay fast and short; the report needs scope and period controls that do not belong on Home.
• Home › At a glance: the counts come from the Inbox as today. The “Oldest: 6–10 working days” line under Waiting for you is the oldest non-empty bucket of pendingByAge from GET /api/v1/dashboards/approvals?scope=me. If that call fails or is slow, show the counts without the line.
• Home › Your unit (right column; on phones after Needs your decision): shown when the person has a unit scope, that is useScopeOptions() returns a unit (a head seat from the team view, or a memo.dashboard.read grant). It calls the same endpoint with scope=unit:<first unit>; pendingByAge, overdue and pendingByPerson are figures for now, so no period is sent. Waiting = sum of pendingByAge; Over 10 days = its last bucket; Most overdue = pendingByPerson with the most overdue (then most pending, then name); with nobody overdue the line says “Nobody is overdue.”. With more units: “You also see … in the dashboard”, each a link to that scope. The card loads on its own (skeleton, then the section error from Page states); Home never waits for it.
• Links: Open the dashboard and the card go to /dashboards/approvals?scope=unit:<id>.
• Sidebar: Dashboard shows only to people with a unit scope (navigation.ts audience: a new kind computed from useTeamAccess() and the memo.dashboard.read grant, instead of signedIn). The address still works for anyone and shows Me.
• Dashboard: with no scope in the address and a unit available, open on the first unit (replace the address with scope=unit:<id>); Me is listed last. Overdue › View list goes to Inbox › Team for a unit, to My tasks for Me.
• Tweak viewer on Home: head (Farhana Rahman, Head of Credit) or approver (Imran Hossain: no card, no Dashboard in the sidebar).
• API: nothing new.
